Preparation of TBDPS-EVR on a Large Scale
A solution of triflate 1b (1.22 kg, 2.83 mol, 2.5 equiv) and PMP (0.53 kg, 3.40 mol, 3 equiv) in acetonitrile (500 mL) was added to a suspension of RAP (1.04 kg, 1.14 mol) in acetonitrile (545 mL), and the reaction mixture was stirred for 24 h at 30 C and 16 h at 20 C. Methanol (11 L) was added, and the reaction mixture was cooled to 2-5 C. A 0.3 M solution of HCl in MeOH (4.5 L) was added to pH 1.9, and the reaction mixture was stirred at this pH for 1.5 h at 2-5 C. A solution of 5% NaHCO3 (0.1 L) was added to adjust the pH to 6.5-7, and the reaction mixture was diluted with water (6.5 L) and extracted with ethyl acetate (13 L, 2   8.5 L). Extracts were dried over Na2SO4, filtered and concentrated under reduced pressure at 35 C, and dried at 10-2 mbar for 2 h. The residue was purified by silica gel (5   5 kg) flash chromatography with hexane and propan-2-ol (gradient from 2 to 5% of propan-2-ol), affording TBDPS-EVR with a purity of more than 95% in 57.8% (0.79 kg) yield.

Aclean, dry, nitrogen-purged 50-L reactor was charged with43 (3.00 kg, 12.5 mol) and 30 L of dichloroethane.Trifluoroacetic anhydride (5.3 L, 38 mol) was then added,and the solution stirred for 1 h at ambient temperature. Aseparate 100-L nitrogen-purged reactor was charged withtriflic acid (650 mL, 8.4 mol) and 30 L of dichloroethaneand warmed to reflux (jacket temperature was 85  C). Thegas outlet from this reactor was passed through a 5% NaOHscrubber. The mixed anhydride in the first reactor was thenadded to the triflic acid/DCE solution over a period of 45min. After the addition, 10 L of trifluoroacetic anhydride/DCE was distilled atmospherically from the reactor, untilthe distillate temperature reached 83  C. The reaction mixturewas cooled and analyzed for cyclization completion byHPLC, which indicated complete conversion to the ethyl esterof the desired product. HCl (30 L, 1 N) was added, and thedichloroethane was removed by distillation at atmosphericpressure. HPLC analysis indicated complete ester hydrolysisto the desired product. The reaction mixture was cooled,diluted with 30 L of brine, and extracted with three portionsof CH2Cl 2 (30, 15, and 15 L, respectively). The combinedorganic extracts were filtered through 4.0 kg of silica gel,rinsing with an additional 16 L CH 2 Cl 2 . The filtrate wasconcentrated at atmospheric pressure to a volume of ca. 15L and gradually displaced with 12 L of methyl tert-butylether, to a final volume of 10 L. The mixture was carefullyquenched by the addition of H 2 O and extracted with CH 2-Cl 2. The organic layer was washed with H 2O and brine andconcentrated after drying. 4-Bromo-5-(trimethylsilyl)furan-2-carbaldehyde (22)

To a dry 250 mL four-neck round-bottom flask (vessel 1) under N2 were added tetrahydrofuran (49 mL, 7.5 L/kg) and diisopropylamine (7.24 mL, 51.4 mmol, 1.2 equiv). The clear solution was cooled to  20  C, and n-butyllithium (2.5 mol/L) in hexanes (18.8 mL, 47.1 mmol, 1.1 equiv) was added over 10 min. The clear solution was cooled to  78  C, and then 3-bromofuran (6.56 g, 42.8 mmol, 1.0 equiv) was added slowly over 10 min between  50 and  78  C, forming a clear yellow solution. This solution was stirred for 1 h at  78  C, over which time a precipitate formed. Chlorotrimethylsilane (6.00 mL, 47.1 mmol, 1.1 equiv) was added dropwise over 10 min, maintaining the temperature below  40  C. The heterogeneous yellow slurry was stirred for 10 min then warmed to room temperature, at which time a clear yellow/orange solution formed. Analysis of this crude reaction mixture by UHPLC-MS indicated >90% yield of (3-bromofuran-2-yl)trimethylsilane (20). Data for the purified product were in accordance with those previously reported: (29) 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3):   0.34 (s, 9H), 6.43 (d, J = 1.8 Hz, 1H), 7.52 (d, J = 1.8 Hz, 1H).
To a separate dry 150 mL three-neck round-bottom flask (vessel 2) under N2 were added tetrahydrofuran (49 mL, 7.5 L/kg) and diisopropylamine (12.1 mL, 85.7 mmol, 2.0 equiv). The clear solution was cooled to  20  C, and n-butyllithium (2.5 mol/L) in hexanes (32.6 mL, 81.4 mmol, 1.9 equiv) was added over 20 min. This clear solution was stirred for 20 min at  20  C before being added to vessel 1 via cannula over 15 min, forming a yellow precipitate. Vessel 1 was stirred for 1.5 h at  78  C before addition of N,N-dimethylformamide (13.3 mL, 171 mmol, 4.0 equiv) over 3 min, forming an orange solution. This solution was warmed slowly to room temperature overnight, forming a yellow suspension. The reaction was quenched with 25% aqueous NH4Cl (60 mL) at room temperature, forming an orange solution that was stirred for 10 min. This reaction mixture was transferred to a separating funnel along with TBME (60 mL). The organic phase was separated, and the aqueous phase was re-extracted (2   60 mL) with TBME. The organic phases were combined and washed with 2 M aqueous H3PO4 (60 mL), water (60 mL) and saturated brine (60 mL), prior to concentration in vacuo to give crude 4-bromo-5-trimethylsilylfuran-2-carbaldehyde (22) (12.4 g, 68% w/w purity, 34.1 mmol, 80% yield), which was taken onto the next step without purification and contained 10% bis-TMS product 21. 1H NMR (500 MHz, DMSO-d6):   0.37 (s, 9H), 7.68 (s, 1H), 9.60 (s, 1H).

The color turned from red to violet and then to black. The addition of the cold Rieke reagent led to cooling of the mixture to approximately 60 C. The residue was cooled to 20 C and diluted with TBME (2 L). The mixture was extracted with 1 N HCl (1 L). The TBME layer was filtered over a pad of Celite (50 g) and Norit (50 g).
